Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36406: test: make p2p_orphan_handling's never-requested checks able to fail

5f22014aca2d071edfea95e8d3d4ba0bebbc57ca test: require an int in PeerTxRelayer.assert_never_requested (Ferdinando Ametrano)
a3c4ad12e92e9d8c0e7c020d49cbdbdef203dfa5 test: make orphan inherit-rejection getdata checks able to fail (Ferdinando Ametrano)

Pull request description:

  `assert_never_requested` compares its argument with the hashes in the node's getdata messages, which are ints. `test_orphan_inherit_rejection` passes it hex strings, so its four checks pass whatever the node requests.

  This passes ints, which needs two more changes. The rejected parent is now relayed from `peer2`: relaying a transaction makes the node request it from that peer (the parent has no witness, so the request is for its txid), and from `peer1` that request would fail the `peer1` check. Mocktime is bumped before the `peer1` and `peer2` checks, because the node requests an orphan's missing parent only after a delay; without the bump those checks would pass before any request could be sent.

  It also fixes a comment: the parent is rejected for its weight (`tx-size`), not its fee.

  To see each check fail, change the scenario so that the node does request the hash. The commit message lists the changes I used.

  Found while porting these tests to https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-node-tests.

  *Made with my usual tools: a computer, the Internet and an LLM. The mistakes, as usual, are all mine.*

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36617: test: Fix intermittent issue in p2p_orphan_handling.py

faf819bf23e8752644695e332cc00413d94af938 test: Fix intermittent issue in p2p_orphan_handling.py (MarcoFalke)

Pull request description:

  Turns out https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/32092 was incomplete and the issue can still happen:

  https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/actions/runs/39809026827/job/119929911875#step:14:14454

  The basic idea is that peer1 disconnects to clear its orphan state. This happens in `DisconnectNodes`->`DeleteNode`->`FinalizeNode`->`TxDownloadManager::DisconnectedPeer`.

  In my prior fix, I assumed that `DisconnectNodes` in the `net` thread would be possible to sync on via a ping-pong. However, the msghand thread may hold a reference to the node, preventing deletion and only moving the node to `m_nodes_disconnected`. Afterward, the `net` thread may hand the pings to the `msghand` thread and go to sleep for a bit.

  Thus, the test proceed and cause a split `getdata`, meaning that `peer2.wait_for_parent_requests([int(parent_peekaboo_AB["txid"], 16), int(parent_missing["txid"], 16)])` fails.

  Fix this by just waiting for `TxDownloadManager::DisconnectedPeer` to have happened via `self.wait_until(lambda: len(node.getorphantxs(verbosity=2)[0]["from"]) == 1)`.

  Edit: Possible diff to reproduce with ~10% failure rate:

  ```diff
  diff --git a/src/net.cpp b/src/net.cpp
  index 1201d3bcb4..e81623484b 100644
  --- a/src/net.cpp
  +++ b/src/net.cpp
  @@ -2229,2 +2229,3 @@ void CConnman::SocketHandlerConnected(const std::vector<CNode*>& nodes,
                       WakeMessageHandler();
  +            UninterruptibleSleep(333ms *m_nodes_disconnected.size());
                   }
  @@ -3261,2 +3262,3 @@ void CConnman::ThreadMessageHandler()
               }
  +            UninterruptibleSleep(33ms);
           }
  ```

  Cmd: `./bld-cmake/test/functional/test_runner.py $(for i in {1..20}; do echo -n "p2p_orphan_handling.py ";done) -j $( nproc )`

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36670: fuzz: check GetStale() returns exactly the stale private broadcast txs

4f3dcb76ab35ed6fe7d81e4997d36333efff12b9 fuzz: check GetStale() returns exactly the stale private broadcast txs (frankomosh)

Pull request description:

  The `private_broadcast` fuzz test checks each tx that `GetStale()` returns. This adds to it by checking that all stale txs are returned.  `ReattemptPrivateBroadcast()` only retries what `GetStale()` returns, and a stale tx left out is never retried.

  This partly came up during review in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35129#pullrequestreview-4427536924, and recently also surfaced in https://mutanthub.space/mutants/3752 , where changing `continue` to `break` in `GetStale()` passes all current tests.

  This PR records when each tx is added and when each node confirms it. Then it checks that `GetStale()` returns exactly the expected txs.

  AFAIU for the external signer stuff it shouldn't matter much whether it's v0 or v2, since users are very unlikely to be using HWI software that doesn't speak v0, but out of caution I've set the external signer PSBT to v0 for the GUI.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36619: rest: don't log an error for /spenttxouts on a block without undo data

eebc145847b4f05da61e95fcae1b420a6ce3ea0f rest: don't log an error for /spenttxouts on a block without undo data (Kanan)

Pull request description:

  `/rest/spenttxouts/<hash>` reads the undo file for every block above genesis. For a block that was stored but never connected (a side branch) or whose undo data was pruned, there is no undo position, so `OpenUndoFile()` fails and `ReadBlockUndo()` writes `OpenUndoFile failed for FlatFilePos(nFile=-1, nPos=0)` to debug.log with `LogError`. The request itself already returns 404, but each unauthenticated request for such a block adds an `[error]` line that looks like disk corruption.

  This checks `CheckBlockDataAvailability()` for `BLOCK_HAVE_UNDO` before reading, so nothing is logged. Pruning clears `BLOCK_HAVE_UNDO`, so pruned blocks are covered too. The response is unchanged.

  The new check at the end of `interface_rest.py` requests a stale block and fails on master because of the logged error.

  Note that the `BlockToJsonVerbosity2` and `BlockToJsonVerbosity3` times were the same.

  - `BlockToJsonVerbosity1`: unchanged

d2645f7ed486718d2af39cf5fc50f46bb8503be9 cmake: Always link `bitcoinqt` to `shlwapi` when building on Windows (Hennadii Stepanov)

Pull request description:

  Building on Windows using Clang instead of the MS compiler may be beneficial, considering the issues with the latter, as outlined in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/31456:

  >    * non-optimized codegen: [build: remove need to test for endianness #29852 (comment)](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29852#issuecomment-2049803970)
  >
  >    * compile failure: [MSVC 17.12.0 internal compiler error  #31303](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/31303)
  >
  >    * ~legal, but brittle stdlib: [util: Drop boost posix_time in ParseISO8601DateTime #31391 (comment)](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/31391#issuecomment-2510762011)~
  >
  >    * unspecified issue: [refactor: Check translatable format strings at compile-time #31061 (comment)](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/31061#issuecomment-2531244463)

  Additionally, MSVC does not [support](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/assembler/inline/inline-assembler) inline assembly on the ARM and x64 processors.

  So this PR:
  1. Closes https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/31456 (and addresses https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/14118).
  2. Could be an alternative to https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/24773.
  3. Closes https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/36153.
  ---

  Additionally, clang-cl:
  1. Produces binaries with [better](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1681) performance. For example:

  | MSVC, block/s | clang-cl, block/s | benchmark |
  |--------------:|------------------:|:----------|
  |          7.40 |             11.52 | `ConnectBlockAllEcdsa`
  |          7.32 |             11.81 | `ConnectBlockAllSchnorr`
  |          7.38 |             11.45 | `ConnectBlockMixedEcdsaSchnorr`
  |         91.86 |            143.12 | `DeserializeAndCheckBlockTest`
  |        121.46 |            189.04 | `DeserializeBlockTest`

  2. Builds faster on the CI:
      - [MSVC](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/actions/runs/13792522864/job/38575846787) - 20m 35s
      - [clang-cl](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/actions/runs/13792522864/job/38575849680) - 12m 43s

  Building on Windows using Clang instead of the MS compiler may be beneficial, considering the issues with the latter, as outlined in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/31456:

  >    * non-optimized codegen: [build: remove need to test for endianness #29852 (comment)](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/29852#issuecomment-2049803970)
  >
  >    * compile failure: [MSVC 17.12.0 internal compiler error  #31303](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/31303)
  >
  >    * ~legal, but brittle stdlib: [util: Drop boost posix_time in ParseISO8601DateTime #31391 (comment)](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/31391#issuecomment-2510762011)~
  >
  >    * unspecified issue: [refactor: Check translatable format strings at compile-time #31061 (comment)](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/31061#issuecomment-2531244463)

  Additionally, MSVC does not [support](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/assembler/inline/inline-assembler) inline assembly on the ARM and x64 processors.

  So this PR:
  1. Closes https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/31456 (and addresses https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/14118).
  2. Could be an alternative to https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/24773.
  3. Closes https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/36153.
  ---

  Additionally, clang-cl:
  1. Produces binaries with [better](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1681) performance. For example:

  | MSVC, block/s | clang-cl, block/s | benchmark |
  |--------------:|------------------:|:----------|
  |          7.40 |             11.52 | `ConnectBlockAllEcdsa`
  |          7.32 |             11.81 | `ConnectBlockAllSchnorr`
  |          7.38 |             11.45 | `ConnectBlockMixedEcdsaSchnorr`
  |         91.86 |            143.12 | `DeserializeAndCheckBlockTest`
  |        121.46 |            189.04 | `DeserializeBlockTest`

  2. Builds faster on the CI:
      - [MSVC](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/actions/runs/13792522864/job/38575846787) - 20m 35s
      - [clang-cl](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/actions/runs/13792522864/job/38575849680) - 12m 43s

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#35041: descriptor: speed-up `Parse` (xpub/xpriv) in ~30%

61cb3d966a855a551307889daea9c45c2c1db203 descriptor: replace O(n) INPUT_CHARSET.find() with precomputed lookup table (brunoerg)
75fd00099ccfa1039df044ca373131e384af1a9d descriptor, key_io: avoid redundant work when parsing keys (brunoerg)

Pull request description:

  This PR speeds up descriptor parsing, for basically descriptors that use xpub/xpriv, through some targeted improvements (I've been working on fuzz targets for wallet stuff for a while. I've noticed that some of them are slow so I started to work on understanding why and improve what can be improved. The finding came from it):

  - Avoid redundant base58 decoding when parsing extended keys (this is the major improvement)

    ParsePubkeyInner unconditionally called both DecodeExtKey() and DecodeExtPubKey(), each running a full DecodeBase58Check (two SHA256 passes over ~111 bytes). A new DecodeExtKeyOrPubKey() function performs a single base58 decode and then checks the prefix, halving the cryptographic work per key. The interfaces of DecodeSecret, DecodeExtKey, and DecodeExtPubKey are also updated to accept string_view instead of const std::string&, eliminating unnecessary string copies in the descriptor parser and allowing DecodeBase58/DecodeBase58Check to use pointer-range iteration instead of strlen.

  - Replace O(n) charset lookup with precomputed table

    DescriptorChecksum previously called std::string::find() for every character in the descriptor string, doing up to 96 comparisons per character. This replaces it with a 256-entry precomputed lookup table for O(1) lookups. The benefit scales with descriptor length.

Pull request description:

  This PR speeds up descriptor parsing, for basically descriptors that use xpub/xpriv, through some targeted improvements (I've been working on fuzz targets for wallet stuff for a while. I've noticed that some of them are slow so I started to work on understanding why and improve what can be improved. The finding came from it):

  - Avoid redundant base58 decoding when parsing extended keys (this is the major improvement)

    ParsePubkeyInner unconditionally called both DecodeExtKey() and DecodeExtPubKey(), each running a full DecodeBase58Check (two SHA256 passes over ~111 bytes). A new DecodeExtKeyOrPubKey() function performs a single base58 decode and then checks the prefix, halving the cryptographic work per key. The interfaces of DecodeSecret, DecodeExtKey, and DecodeExtPubKey are also updated to accept string_view instead of const std::string&, eliminating unnecessary string copies in the descriptor parser and allowing DecodeBase58/DecodeBase58Check to use pointer-range iteration instead of strlen.

  - Replace O(n) charset lookup with precomputed table

    DescriptorChecksum previously called std::string::find() for every character in the descriptor string, doing up to 96 comparisons per character. This replaces it with a 256-entry precomputed lookup table for O(1) lookups. The benefit scales with descriptor length.

commit.message:
p2p: clean up a 1p1c package child that is already in the mempool

An orphan that enters the mempool other than through peer relay (e.g. by
RPC) stays in the orphanage, so Find1P1CPackage can pick it as the child
of a reconsiderable parent, and package evaluation then reports it as
MEMPOOL_ENTRY, which hits Assume(false). Have Find1P1CPackage erase such
children from the orphanage and skip them.

Match by txid, so an orphan whose different-witness version is in the
mempool is also erased rather than evaluated in a package it cannot
enter.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36344: wallet: reject duplicate inputs in sendall

654a92a9d3e76f3ff4ec4975f4fbcfba1a6091be wallet: reject duplicate inputs in sendall (Bruce0X)

Pull request description:

  `sendall` with the `inputs` option doesn't check for duplicates. Each listed input is added to `total_input_value` in the loop at spend.cpp:1472, so passing the same UTXO twice counts its value twice.

  On regtest, with a wallet that has a single 1 BTC UTXO:

  ```
  sendall '["<addr>"]' '{"inputs": [<utxo>, <utxo>]}'
  ```

  - the RPC returns `complete: true`
  - the committed tx has 2 inputs (the same outpoint twice) and one output of 1.99998230 BTC
  - it isn't in the mempool, and `testmempoolaccept` rejects it with `bad-txns-inputs-duplicate`
  - after that, `listunspent` is empty and `getbalances` shows `nonmempool: -1.0` until the tx is abandoned

  `send` and `walletcreatefundedpsbt` aren't affected, because `CCoinControl::Select` removes duplicates.

  This rejects a duplicated input with `Invalid parameter, duplicated input: <txid>:<vout>` (RPC_INVALID_PARAMETER). The message matches what `createrawtransaction` says for duplicated addresses. The new `sendall_fails_on_duplicate_input` test fails on master ("No exception raised") and passes with the fix. `wallet_send.py` still passes.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36584: kernel: make btck_LogEntry opaque

b2c077394a585a4155bd9d7a28b9b7c7553c9dc5 kernel: make btck_LogEntry opaque (stickies-v)

Pull request description:

  Makes `btck_LogEntry` an opaque type with `btck_log_entry_get_*` accessors, instead of a public struct. This allows adding or changing fields without breaking the ABI, and is consistent with ~all other kernel objects. Follow-up to https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34374#discussion_r4207440088.

  I added a benchmark in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/compare/master...stickies-v:bitcoin:2026-10/kernel-logentry-bench, and found that performance is not meaningfully impacted either way. Some results below.

  <details>
  <summary>Performance stats</summary>

  ### Performance

  Fields are now converted only when read, at the cost of a library call per field. The [benchmark](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/compare/master...stickies-v:bitcoin:2026-10/kernel-logentry-bench) measures a kernel log statement up to and including the callback (Apple M4 Pro, static library, `-O2`, median of 2×25 interleaved runs):

  | Callback reads | master | PR | Delta |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|
  | no fields | 57.4 ns | 55.2 ns | −1.6 to −2.5 ns |
  | message only | 57.8 ns | 56.0 ns | −1.4 to −2.0 ns |
  | all 9 fields | 57.9 ns | 62.7 ns | +4.8 to +5.4 ns |

  Break-even is at 2-3 fields. Either way, the difference is small next to the ~50 ns the log statement costs before the callback, and to what a consumer typically does with the entry (formatting, I/O).
  </details>

b2c077394a585a4155bd9d7a28b9b7c7553c9dc5 kernel: make btck_LogEntry opaque (stickies-v)

Pull request description:

  Makes `btck_LogEntry` an opaque type with `btck_log_entry_get_*` accessors, instead of a public struct. This allows adding or changing fields without breaking the ABI, and is consistent with ~all other kernel objects. Follow-up to https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34374#discussion_r4207440088.

  I added a benchmark in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/compare/master...stickies-v:bitcoin:2026-10/kernel-logentry-bench, and found that performance is not meaningfully impacted either way. Some results below.

  <details>
  <summary>Performance stats</summary>

  ### Performance

  Fields are now converted only when read, at the cost of a library call per field. The [benchmark](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/compare/master...stickies-v:bitcoin:2026-10/kernel-logentry-bench) measures a kernel log statement up to and including the callback (Apple M4 Pro, static library, `-O2`, median of 2×25 interleaved runs):

  | Callback reads | master | PR | Delta |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|
  | no fields | 57.4 ns | 55.2 ns | −1.6 to −2.5 ns |
  | message only | 57.8 ns | 56.0 ns | −1.4 to −2.0 ns |
  | all 9 fields | 57.9 ns | 62.7 ns | +4.8 to +5.4 ns |

  Break-even is at 2-3 fields. Either way, the difference is small next to the ~50 ns the log statement costs before the callback, and to what a consumer typically does with the entry (formatting, I/O).
  </details>

commit.message:
wallet: reject duplicate inputs in sendall

sendall with the inputs option adds up the value of each listed input
without checking for duplicates. When the same UTXO is given twice, the
input value is counted twice, and the wallet builds, signs and commits
a transaction that spends one outpoint twice and pays out twice its
value. The RPC reports success, but the transaction is consensus-invalid
(bad-txns-inputs-duplicate), and the coin disappears from listunspent
until the transaction is abandoned.

Reject duplicated inputs with an error, like createrawtransaction does
for duplicated addresses.

(required for cl.exe) to 2026 18.7, the first release whose bundled
LLVM (22.1.3) includes the following bugfix:

Couple `BSWAP_CONSTEXPR` definition to bswap implementation

Previously `BSWAP_CONSTEXPR` was defined empty whenever `_MSC_VER` was
defined. However, clang-cl also defines `_MSC_VER` while it selects
Clang's `__builtin_bswap*` builtins, which are `constexpr`.

commit.message:
cmake: Adjust diagnostic flags for clang-cl

Being compatible with cl.exe, clang-cl supports most of the same
command-line options. These options are typically guarded by the `MSVC`
CMake variable.

Options not supported by clang-cl, such as `/wdNNN`, are now guarded by
`CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID STREQUAL "MSVC"`.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36305: net: Use exclusive P2P listen sockets on Windows

db31a3ad1f75538d07707d373adbfbe90ba8e328 test: check P2P listen port exclusivity (winterrdog)
0dbd271eb4a3263b8b81ccf22876429076bae574 net: use exclusive P2P listen sockets on Windows (winterrdog)

Pull request description:

  on Windows, `SO_REUSEADDR` does not carry over the same semantics as on
  POSIX systems. a second socket can set `SO_REUSEADDR` and bind to a
  port that is _already in use_ by another process running under
  the _same_ user account. this means another local process could bind to
  the P2P listen port and receive incoming connections intended for
  `bitcoind`.

  this matters because the P2P listener is expected to have exclusive
  ownership of its address and port. allowing another process to bind to
  it could let that process _intercept_ incoming P2P connections. this is
  in a similar spirit to #36169, which made the RPC listener exclusive on
  Windows.

  to fix this, we use `SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE` for the P2P listen socket on
  Windows instead of `SO_REUSEADDR`, while retaining `SO_REUSEADDR` on
  other platforms. the added test verifies the expected behaviour by
  attempting to bind a second socket to the same port. on Windows, this
  fails with `WSAEACCES` (`10013`), which Python exposes as
  `PermissionError` (an `OSError` subclass).

  references:

  - https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winsock/using-so-reuseaddr-and-so-exclusiveaddruse
  - https://stackoverflow.com/questions/14388706/how-do-so-reuseaddr-and-so-reuseport-differ/14388707#14388707

Pull request description:

  If the `<<` operator exists, boost can use this as a debug output when a check fails (besides `BOOST_CHECK`). This adds `<<` for types commonly used across the unit tests that do not yet have a display output. Each callsite that uses these types are then updated to use macros that will print the debug output on failure. All of these display strings would be used as part of #35713, but we can also use them with boost today.

  What this PR does:
  - Adds debug output for types used across multiple files, or types that have a clear debug string, and migrates the `BOOST_CHECK` calls. This covers the majority of custom types that did not yet have a debug string.

  What this PR does _not_ do:
  - Migrate `BOOST_CHECK` callsites for types that already _do_ have a debug output (all primitive type comparisons, `CFeeRate`, etc). This would be a much larger refactor and could perhaps be done after.
  - Add debug output for `std::vector<T>` where `T` is streamable. These can be migrated to `BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL_COLLECTIONS`, but is a similar refactor to the one above.
  - Add debug output for `std::vector<unsigned char>` and related. Also a large refactor, and could use discussion.
  - Add debug output for types that would require a `friend` method in the source code (`ByRatio`)

commit.message:
rpc: Properly throw on internal FindTx IO errors in ProcessPSBT and GetTransaction

Currently, the FindTx return value is an optional, where nullopt
represents two different outcomes: I/O error and missing tx.

One may argue that this is fine in ProcessPSBT, because a -txindex
lookup error is rare, and an error where the fallbacks to lookup the tx
are also failing is even rarer. However, a -txindex corruption may also
point to a larger system corruption and it seems better to notify the
user properly by throwing an exception.

If I/O errors should be ignored in the future, it would be trivial to
catch them here. However, that decision should be up to the
caller, and not enforced by the low-level function.

Do the same for GetTransaction:
Currently the GetTransaction return value is a nullable transaction
pointer, where nullptr represents two different outcomes: I/O error and
missing tx.

Reporting a confirmed transaction as missing is wrong, so properly
return an error instead.

Pull request description:

  **Problem:** The four-argument `CBloomFilter` constructor is used by unit tests and the fuzz target to exercise Bloom filter sizing directly.
  Zero elements make the hash-function calculation divide by zero.
  The size calculation converts its floating-point result to `unsigned int` before applying the protocol limit, which is undefined for zero or invalid false-positive rates and for valid parameters whose calculated size exceeds the integer range.

  Clamp the calculated size before its integer conversion so large valid inputs remain within the protocol limit.

commit.message:
rpc: Return proper error messages from getrawtransaction

When a block hash is passed in and the block can't be read, the RPC
reports "No such transaction found in the provided block", even though
the block was never searched. Fix this by throwing an I/O error from
GetTransaction when ReadBlock fails.

Because the not-found branch no longer runs when the read fails, check
block availability up front with CheckBlockDataAvailability. This also
gives more specific errors for pruned and not yet downloaded blocks
than the previous "Block not available".

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36594: net: make orphan reconsideration more granular

83003cafaa81bb116526419246608658ede824b6 qa: test a single orphan is processed per peer turn, regardless of its validation result (Antoine Poinsot)
28a41e61ab5d993d344dc5c8180482eb146c6bd5 net: reconsider at most one orphan per call, whatever the validation result (Antoine Poinsot)

Pull request description:

  We currently concentrate the validation of all the assigned peer’s reconsiderable orphans that are still missing inputs in a single message-processing turn. This ties orphan processing to validation result, and adds latency to processing other peers' messages.

  Always process a single reconsiderable orphan per turn instead. This removes the need for an immediate validation result, and shifts the latency from other peers to the assigned peer.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36682: refactor: Use std::erase and std::erase_if

fa87bfe31dfda2d102c4e0cb5d39813cf84c7d1e refactor: Use std::erase and std::erase_if over iterator-based erase (MarcoFalke)

Pull request description:

  Convert `remove` and `remove_if` to the C++20 `std::erase` and `std::erase_if` overloads.

  The legacy ones can be confusing, because:

  * Array-based containers (like vector) must use the erase-remove idiom. Forgetting the erase, or forgetting to pass the end iterator (`bugprone-inaccurate-erase`) can be a bug, see also https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36588#discussion_r4345799022. So a call only to "remove" will not erase.
  * Node-based containers (like list or set) must not use the idiom. Using it will be a pessimization or won't compile. And correctly not using the idiom reads confusing, because a call to "remove" will actually erase.
  * They are more verbose.

  Also convert simple iterator-erase (which is verbose, but fine) to the std overload.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#35714: validation: return block-file flush errors

12f691cf286ea9a020583d267b94efca102a4056 validation: return block-file flush errors (Lőrinc)
07d23eb75527b8dd6571a33b3bc304815764bc07 test: characterize writes after flush failure (Lőrinc)

Pull request description:

  **Problem:** When flushing block or undo data fails, `FlushStateToDisk()` still writes block-index metadata and coins data, then advances `m_last_flushed_block`.
  With a separate `-blocksdir`, persistent failures there can leave metadata referring to block data that is not durable even when chainstate writes succeed.

test: wait for the node to finish the last block in p2p_ping_ibd

ProcessBlock() stamps m_last_block_time only after ProcessNewBlock() returns, so getblockcount
can show the new height, with nothing in flight, before the stamp is taken. A bumpmocktime in
that gap stamps the block with the bumped time, and the final bump then leaves the ping timeout
exactly at its boundary, where it never fires. Sync with a ping after the last block, so the
node has finished processing it before the clock moves.

The race has been present since the test was added in #36080.
